scope: Current Look parent/scroll-row/wrapping named viewport and its existing scrollbar target connection only.

decompiler.normalization: Trim trailing whitespace and final blank lines only

limitations: The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
Pseudocode is Ghidra decompiler output, not original source and not text-equivalent to Hopper output.
External functions and functions without an analyzable body return null; other decompiler failures remain explicit.
macOS sessions require a matching executable Ghidra native decompiler; REA checks for it but does not build native components or change Gatekeeper quarantine state.
Headerless raw-binary analysis uses the caller-supplied architecture and entry address; file offset 0 is mapped at that address. Headers are not discovered from file bytes.

Little-endian generic Ghidra languages are used for x86, x86_64, arm, arm64, and NMOS 6502. Big-endian, Thumb-only, Cortex-M, 65C02, 65816, and other processor variants are unsupported in this increment.
Static analysis does not emulate reset vectors, memory-mapped I/O, or firmware boot sequences.

static_validation: Six poison-seeded current native Node captures, original byte/literal/query commitments, two source callers and actual named-target/scrollbar connection; Rust syntax parses.
limits: Raw Ghidra function imports omit external callee bodies and original referenced data; pseudocode uses inferred signatures.
Current native data are read independently by Node replay, with explicit memcpy and UI-publication seams.
The common wheel/drag implementation is reused; its complete current native scheduling/aliases are not certified.
No compilation, rebuilt source/UI/input execution, gameplay or original/rebuilt comparison.
